title: Diagonal-class normalization of the intrinsic proper polynomial comparisons
statement:
Let $S$ be an arbitrary scheme and $f:X\to S$ a proper, flat morphism of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Write $K_f=f^!\mathcal O_S$, with its adjunction trace and its canonical polynomial comparisons, for the object of [lem-sfb-proper-flat-dualizing-polynomial-model], in the quasi-coherent derived category [def-pc-derived-category], with derived pullback [def-pc-derived-pullback]. The intrinsic pair of that theorem has a specified diagonal class $\xi_f$, so $(K_f,\xi_f)$ is a coherent relative dualizing pair [def-trf-coherent-relative-dualizing-pair]. This class and the canonical comparisons satisfy the following normalization statements.
For every affine open $V\subset S$, let $f_V:X_V=f^{-1}(V)\to V$ and let $a_V$ be a right adjoint of $Rf_{V,*}$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. The unique trace-preserving identification $K_f|_{X_V}\simeq a_V(\mathcal O_V)$ carries $\xi_f|_{X_V\times_VX_V}$ to the canonical class $\xi_{a_V}$ of [lem-sfb-proper-adjoint-diagonal-pair].
For every $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X_V$, and surjection $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow B$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], put $C_P=C_B^P(\Omega^n_{P/R}[n])$ with its coinduction $B$-action [def-trf-derived-coinduction], [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. Let $Q=B\otimes_RB$, $p_1(b)=b\otimes1$, and let $\xi_P:B\to C_P\otimes_{B,p_1}^{\mathbf L}Q$ be the arbitrary-ring graph-evaluation class of [lem-sfb-arbitrary-polynomial-graph-class-base-change]. Under the affine derived equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], $(C_P,\xi_P)$ realizes a coherent relative dualizing pair on $U/V$. The canonical comparison $\alpha_P:K_f|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde C_P$ of [lem-sfb-proper-flat-dualizing-polynomial-model] satisfies
$$(Lp_1^*\alpha_P)(\xi_f|_{U\times_VU})=\widetilde\xi_P.$$
It is the unique isomorphism with this equation. Here $p_1:U\times_VU\to U$ on the displayed equation is the first projection, and tildes denote the affine realization; the preceding ring coprojection defines its module pullback. These assertions hold for every such chart and every proper flat finitely presented $f$ over an arbitrary base, and refer to the specified canonical comparisons, with no freedom to multiply them by chart-dependent units. No comparison between two base schemes and no identification of a proper trace-pair base-change map with a polynomial exchange is asserted.
The specified construction in this statement is fixed as follows. The trace on $K_f$ is identified with the proper trace pair of [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-duality], using [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence]; the diagonal class is constructed from the local adjunctions and glued. On a chart put $M=R\Gamma(U,K_f|_U)$ and let $\gamma:B[0]\to M\otimes_{B,p_1}^{\mathbf L}Q$ be that class under affine realization. Identify $\Omega^n_{P/R}$ with $P$ by the ordered volume $dt_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dt_n$. Taking $H^0$ of [lem-sfb-arbitrary-polynomial-diagonal-hom] gives a $B$-linear natural representing bijection
$$\psi_T:\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Q)}(B[0],T\otimes_{B,p_1}^{\mathbf L}Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(C_P,T).$$
Put $w=\psi_{C_P}(\xi_P)$ and $e=\psi_M(\gamma)\circ w^{-1}:C_P\to M$. The construction takes $\alpha_P$ to be the affine realization of $e^{-1}$. The assertions include that $w$ and $e$ are invertible and that this prescription is independent of the auxiliary representing bijection $\psi$. This specifies the meaning of the canonical arrows, which otherwise are not determined by the polynomial-refinement and restriction rules alone.

source.place: Tags 0E2Z (lemma-flat-proper-relative-dualizing), 0E2W (lemma-uniqueness-relative-dualizing), 0E4P (remark-relative-dualizing-complex-bis), and 0BV2 (remark-local-calculation-shriek). proof.text: First identify the trace, without using polynomial comparisons. Let $(K^0,\tau^0)$ be the proper space trace pair, transported to the Zariski category. On every affine base $V$, its Hom characterization identifies $K^0|_{X_V}$ with $a_V(\mathcal O_V)$, with the adjunction trace. These are qcqs schemes since $X_V$ is proper over affine $V$. The adjoint tensor formula identifies $Lf_V^*(-)\otimes K^0|_{X_V}$ with $a_V$, including its counit. The local adjunction criterion gives $Rf_*\dashv (Lf^*(-)\otimes K^0)$ on the arbitrary base $S$. The model theorem already supplies $Rf_*\dashv f^!$. The two representing Hom bijections give the unique counit-preserving isomorphism between these right adjoints; at $\mathcal O_S$ it gives $K^0\simeq K_f$, preserving trace. Consequently $h_V:K_f|_{X_V}\simeq a_V(\mathcal O_V)$ is the trace-preserving identification, and these identifications are compatible on affine refinements of base-open overlaps. Apply the proper-adjoint diagonal theorem on $V$ and transport its class backwards by $h_V$. Write this local class as $\zeta_V$. That theorem says both that the local pair is coherent and that trace-preserving adjoint identifications preserve its class.

proof.text: Put $Y=X\times_SX$, $D=\Delta_*\mathcal O_X[0]$ and $H=R\mathcal Hom_Y(D,Lp_1^*K_f)$. The opens $Y_V=X_V\times_VX_V$ cover $Y$, since every point has an image in some affine $V\subset S$. Restriction of derived internal Hom, restriction of the first-projection pullback, and the multiplication isomorphism of each local pair give $H|_{Y_V}\simeq D|_{Y_V}$. Hence $H$ has cohomology only in degree zero. The derived-Hom/global-sections identification, in its open-restriction-compatible form (an isomorphism of presheaves $U\mapsto H^0(U,H)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_U)}(D|_U,Lp_1^*K_f|_U)$), now identifies morphisms $D\to Lp_1^*K_f$ over $Y$ and over each $Y_V$ with sections of $\mathcal H^0H$, compatibly with restriction: indeed a nonnegative injective resolution of the degree-zero sheaf computes $H^0R\Gamma$ as its ordinary sections. On an overlap $V\cap W$, cover the base intersection by affine opens; Step 1 and the base-open compatibility clause of the proper-adjoint theorem identify the restrictions of $\zeta_V$ and $\zeta_W$. Their sections therefore glue to a unique $\xi_f$. The multiplication map is invertible on every $Y_V$, hence globally. Pseudo-coherence and local relative Tor amplitude hold on the source cover $X_V$ by the local pairs. Thus $(K_f,\xi_f)$ is coherent. By construction $h_V$ carries its restriction to $\xi_{a_V}$. No intersection of affine opens has been assumed affine, and no finite cover of $S$ has been used.

Fix a chart. Apply arbitrary-base affine realization to the supplied pair of Step 2, taking both its input pairs equal to $(K_f,\xi_f)$. It gives the flat finitely presented map $R\to B$, an $R$-perfect complex $M$, and the actual class $\gamma:B\to M_1$, with multiplication $B\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_Q(B,M_1)$. Here $T_1=T\otimes_{B,p_1}^{\mathbf L}Q$. The arbitrary polynomial-dual properties give $R$-perfect $C_P$ and the scalar isomorphism $B\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_B(C_P,C_P)$, after identifying $\Omega^n$ with $P$ by its ordered volume. The arbitrary-ring graph-class theorem supplies the actual $\xi_P$ and its multiplication isomorphism $B\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_Q(B,(C_P)_1)$. Applying the unmarked relative-dualizing isomorphism theorem to $M,C_P$ therefore supplies some isomorphism $a:C_P\xrightarrow{\sim}M$. It is used only to test invertibility below; it is not taken as the canonical comparison.

proof.text: The two multiplication isomorphisms in Step 3 identify the modules $F(C_P)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Q)}(B,(C_P)_1)$ and $F(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Q)}(B,M_1)$ with $B$, sending $\xi_P$ and $\gamma$ respectively to their unit generators. This follows by taking $H^0$: multiplication by the class sends $b$ to precomposition of the class by multiplication by $b$. The polynomial-diagonal Hom theorem, with its first-coprojection restriction and the ordered-volume identification, gives a $B$-linear natural representing bijection $\psi_T:F(T)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(C_P,T)$. The scalar isomorphism of Step 3 gives $\operatorname{End}(C_P)=B$; hence $w=\psi_{C_P}(\xi_P)$ is a generator of this rank-one module, so is multiplication by a unit. Also $\operatorname{Hom}(C_P,M)$ is free rank one with basis $a$ from Step 3. Thus $\psi_M(\gamma)$ is a unit times $a$, and $e=\psi_M(\gamma)\circ w^{-1}$ is invertible. Only invertibility of a generator of the regular module $B$ is used: if $Bw=B$, write $bw=1$; commutativity gives $wb=1$.

source.place: Tag 0A65 (lemma-internal-hom); elementary generator argument after the cited derived-category isomorphisms

proof.text:
For every $u:C_P\to T$, naturality of $\psi$ gives the explicit equation
$$\psi_T((u\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{B,p_1}Q)\xi_P)=u\circ w.$$
Since $w$ is invertible, the map $u\mapsto(u\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q)\xi_P$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}(C_P,T)$ to $F(T)$. At $T=M$, the construction $e=\psi_M(\gamma)w^{-1}$ is therefore its unique inverse image of $\gamma$. In particular
$$(e\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q)\xi_P=\gamma,\qquad (e^{-1}\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q)\gamma=\xi_P.$$
The displayed bijection is defined using only the specified graph class and tensoring; its inverse is unique. Thus replacing $\psi$ by any other $B$-linear natural representing bijection produces exactly the same $e$. This proves independence without assuming that an unspecified natural isomorphism already has the graph normalization.

source.place: Elementary naturality/Yoneda calculation with the representing bijection constructed in Step 4

proof.text:
Realize $e^{-1}:M\to C_P$ on $U$. This is the specified construction of $\alpha_P$. Affine realization in Step 3 identifies $\gamma$ with $\xi_f|_{U\times_VU}$; the canonical affine derived pullback/tensor comparison identifies sheafification of $e^{-1}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{B,p_1}Q$ with $Lp_1^*\alpha_P$. Applying associated sheaf to the second equation of Step 5 gives precisely
$$(Lp_1^*\alpha_P)(\xi_f|_{U\times_VU})=\widetilde\xi_P.$$
Moreover $\widetilde C_P\simeq K_f|_U$, so it has the required finiteness properties. The multiplication maps of the two classes are conjugate under this isomorphism: transposing $\xi_f\circ\mu$ and then applying $Lp_1^*\alpha_P$ is the same as transposing $(Lp_1^*\alpha_P)\xi_f\circ\mu$, by naturality of tensor--Hom. Consequently multiplication by $\widetilde\xi_P$ is invertible. Thus $(\widetilde C_P,\widetilde\xi_P)$ is a coherent pair on $U/V$.

proof.text: Apply supplied-pair open rigidity on $U/V$ to the pairs in Steps 2 and 6. It gives uniqueness of the isomorphism satisfying the displayed class equation; existence is already the computed $\alpha_P$. In particular multiplying a comparison by $b\in B^\times$ would multiply its target class by $b$, and the generator property in Step 4 forces $b=1$. The same argument applies to every chart independently, with the fixed adjunction trace and the ordered graph volume; no chart-dependent scalar choices remain. The empty open is included by open rigidity. For $B=0$ all the relevant objects and Hom modules are zero and all maps are unique isomorphisms; the zero ring has its unique unit. For $n=0$ the volume is $1$, its shift is zero and the graph tuple is empty, as included in the graph-class theorem. All invoked algebraic theorems allow arbitrary rings. No base-change comparison between distinct base schemes is used to identify a proper polynomial arrow.
